library_preparation_preflight.summary: javacv ships zero native binaries; its wrapper classes load natives in static initializers, so any real use (even trivial construction of FFmpegFrameGrabber/OpenCVFrameConverter-style classes) needs classified native jars for opencv/ffmpeg/openblas on the test classpath or it fails with UnsatisfiedLinkError under both JVM and Native Image.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: javacv's own Maven coordinate carries no native binaries by design (see bytedeco/javacv README: use javacv-platform or add classified deps / -Djavacpp.platform). Keep generated tests inside the functionality covered by the three natives pre-added above (video/image grab, decode, Mat<->BufferedImage conversion, e.g. via FFmpegFrameGrabber, OpenCVFrameConverter, Java2DFrameConverter). Avoid classes tied to submodules whose native jars are NOT present: flycapture, libdc1394, libfreenect/libfreenect2, librealsense/librealsense2, videoinput, artoolkitplus (hardware camera drivers, unusable in CI anyway) and leptonica/tesseract (OCR) — exercising those will hit the same UnsatisfiedLinkError pattern unless their linux-x86_64 classifiers are added too. A small bundled test resource (short video or image file) will likely be needed as input for FrameGrabber-style tests since there's no camera/display in CI.
risks: This assessment is based on POM/README research, not a local Gradle/Native Image run; if the eventual generated test ends up needing tesseract/leptonica or a different native module, the missing classifier will surface the same way and need the identical fix (add that module's linux-x86_64 classified testImplementation dependency).

Native Image may additionally need javacpp's bundled shared libraries registered as resources (they ship under classpath paths like /org/bytedeco/<module>/linux-x86_64/); local native-image verification is authoritative on whether extra resource-config is needed beyond the dependency itself.
